_**User**_

Fix this bug...

The `ShellSession::execute_command_direct` method takes ownership of the stdout/stderr pipes from the child process. This design forces the bash process to be respawned after *every* command execution. Consequently, all session state (e.g., current directory, environment variables, command history) is lost between commands, defeating the purpose of a persistent shell session and introducing significant performance overhead.
